To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the development of personalized cancer diagnostics and treatments requires new approaches to HTA.
personalized medicine is a promising field of health care, but it also presents new challenges for HTA.
personalized medicine calls for novel health technology assessment ( HTA ) concepts and methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of innovative diagnostic and treatment methods in the context of personalized health care.
the development of a new HTA concept that can assess the evidence for the clinical utility of personalized medicine and its impact on public health.
the development of a new generation of HTA that is able to deal with personalized health care.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current HTA models are not adequate to address the needs and challenges of personalized health care.
HTA needs a new paradigm for personalized health care, and that this new paradigm needs to be developed.
the development of novel assessment methods is a prerequisite for the successful implementation of personalized health care in the public sector.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current HTA system needs further development to be able to deal adequately with the new developments in health care.
we need to rethink HTA in the context of personalized medicine.
we need to develop a new generation of health technology assessment (NG-CTA).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the development and implementation of new technologies in the field of genomics and personalized medicine will require a new generation of assessment models.
the current HTA models are not sufficient to assess the value of personalized medicine and to provide guidance for decision making.
the current state of HTA cannot be used to assess the evidence generated in the IG-Mutanomics project and other similar research projects.
